shortDescription: Czech manufacturing business sentiment jumped to more than a four-year high in August amid strong output and orders, the S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index showed on Thursday.

children: Czech manufacturing business sentiment jumped to more than a four-year high in August amid strong output and orders, the S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index showed on Thursday.
The headline PMI rose to 54.1 in August from 52.2 in July, marking the strongest reading since April 2022 and moving further above the 50 mark that divides expansion from contraction.
Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast a reading of 52.6.
"Stronger client interest drove a steep rise in new orders and a solid increase in production levels," the survey compilers wrote.
"Despite firms registering a fresh round of hiring, backlogs continued to accumulate, and at the quickest pace since December 2021."
